newsitem.title: INDIA: NOKIA SEES JUMP IN INDIA MOBILE PHONES.
newsitem.headline: NOKIA SEES JUMP IN INDIA MOBILE PHONES.

text.p: India is expected to have nearly 750,000 mobile phone users by the end of 1997, more than triple the 260,000 users at the end of 1996, a senior official of Nokia Pvt Ltd, a unit of Finland's Nokia Oy, said on Monday.

"Our prediction is that the Indian market will add 500,000 to 550,000 users in 1997, and will stand at about 750,000 by the end of the year," Parikshit Bhasin, joint managing director, Nokia Pvt Ltd, told Reuters after a news conference.

He said the market had received a boost with mobile phone services having started in India's regional telephone zones. Increased sales of handsets in large cities and a fall in the number of smuggled handsets had also aided the trend, he said.
Mobile phones debuted in India in October 1995 in four cities -- Delhi, Bombay, Madras and Calcutta -- following an auction of cellular service licences by the government in 1992.
Regional licences for other zones were auctioned in 1995, and services began in most regions early this year.
Bhasin said the key growth centres were still the four large cities, where cellular phones had become a business tool, and demand was steadily increasing.
He added Nokia expected similar growth in the regions in the second quarter of 1998.
Meanwhile, handset vendors had cut prices to smother the temptation of going for smuggled goods, Bhasin said.
"Last year Nokia launched its 1610 model at 20,000 rupees ($558.65) and its 8110 model at 42,000 rupees. Today, the 1610 costs 13,000 rupees and the 8110, 30,000 rupees," he said.
Bhasin said nearly 80 percent of all mobile phones available in India were priced below 15,000 rupees.
Bhasin was speaking after the launch of Nokia's latest handphone, 3810, which costs 18,125 rupees and has been specially designed for Asia-Pacific consumers.
-- Sanjit Singh, New Delhi Newsroom (91) 11-301-2024; Fax (91) 11-301-4043
